lines.text: Three, nine, twenty-seven, eighty-one. Powers of three grow fast!
lines.caption: Three, nine, twenty-seven, eighty-one. Powers of three grow fast!

lines.text: Can one of them ever end in zero one? <short pause> Let's find out.
lines.caption: Can one of them ever end in zero one? Let's find out.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack it together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack it together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: What is the smallest positive whole number n, so three to the n ends in zero one?
lines.caption: What is the smallest positive whole number n, so three to the n ends in zero one?

lines.text: The choices are four, ten, twenty, forty and one hundred. Take a good look.
lines.caption: The choices are four, ten, twenty, forty and one hundred. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what are we really asking?
lines.caption: So what are we really asking?

lines.text: Keep multiplying by three. We want the last two digits to be zero, then one.
lines.caption: Keep multiplying by three. We want the last two digits to be zero, then one.

lines.text: And we want the FIRST power where that happens.
lines.caption: And we want the FIRST power where that happens.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's start small, with just the last digit.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's start small, with just the last digit.

lines.text: Here's a handy fact. A product's last digit depends only on the last digits you multiply.
lines.caption: Here's a handy fact. A product's last digit depends only on the last digits you multiply.

lines.text: Three, then nine. Nine times three is twenty-seven, so the last digit is seven.
lines.caption: Three, then nine. Nine times three is twenty-seven, so the last digit is seven.

lines.text: Seven times three is twenty-one, so one. And one times three is three again.
lines.caption: Seven times three is twenty-one, so one. And one times three is three again.

lines.text: The last digits go three, nine, seven, one, and then repeat. A loop of four!
lines.caption: The last digits go three, nine, seven, one, and then repeat. A loop of four!

lines.text: So three to the n ends in one only for n equals four, eight, twelve, and so on.
lines.caption: So three to the n ends in one only for n equals four, eight, twelve, and so on.

lines.text: That shrinks our search a lot! Now let's test those powers, in order.
lines.caption: That shrinks our search a lot! Now let's test those powers, in order.

lines.text: Same trick for two digits: only the last two digits matter. The rest are just hundreds.
lines.caption: Same trick for two digits: only the last two digits matter. The rest are just hundreds.

lines.text: Three to the fourth is eighty-one. It ends in one, but not zero one. Not yet!
lines.caption: Three to the fourth is eighty-one. It ends in one, but not zero one. Not yet!

lines.text: To jump four more powers, we multiply by eighty-one.
lines.caption: To jump four more powers, we multiply by eighty-one.

lines.text: Eighty-one times eighty-one ends in sixty-one. That's three to the eighth.
lines.caption: Eighty-one times eighty-one ends in sixty-one. That's three to the eighth.

lines.text: Sixty-one times eighty-one ends in forty-one. That's three to the twelfth.
lines.caption: Sixty-one times eighty-one ends in forty-one. That's three to the twelfth.

lines.text: Forty-one times eighty-one ends in twenty-one. That's three to the sixteenth.
lines.caption: Forty-one times eighty-one ends in twenty-one. That's three to the sixteenth.

lines.text: Notice the pattern? The tens digit drops by two every time.
lines.caption: Notice the pattern? The tens digit drops by two every time.

lines.text: Twenty-one times eighty-one ends in <short pause> zero one! That's three to the twentieth.
lines.caption: Twenty-one times eighty-one ends in zero one! That's three to the twentieth.

lines.text: So the smallest n is twenty. The answer is C!
lines.caption: So the smallest n is twenty. The answer is C!

lines.text: Here's a clever second way. Think of eighty-one as eighty plus one.
lines.caption: Here's a clever second way. Think of eighty-one as eighty plus one.

lines.text: So times eighty-one means: times eighty, plus one more copy of the number.
lines.caption: So times eighty-one means: times eighty, plus one more copy of the number.

lines.text: Our numbers all end in one. Anything ending in one, times eighty, ends in eighty.
lines.caption: Our numbers all end in one. Anything ending in one, times eighty, ends in eighty.

lines.text: So each time we multiply by eighty-one, we just ADD eighty to the last two digits!
lines.caption: So each time we multiply by eighty-one, we just ADD eighty to the last two digits!

lines.text: Start at three to the zero, which is one. Every jump of four powers adds another eighty.
lines.caption: Start at three to the zero, which is one. Every jump of four powers adds another eighty.

lines.text: We need the eighties to add up to a number ending in zero zero.
lines.caption: We need the eighties to add up to a number ending in zero zero.

lines.text: Eighty, one hundred sixty, two hundred forty, three hundred twenty, <short pause> four hundred!
lines.caption: Eighty, one hundred sixty, two hundred forty, three hundred twenty, four hundred!

lines.text: Four hundred is five eighties. Five jumps of four powers is twenty. Three to the twentieth again!
lines.caption: Four hundred is five eighties. Five jumps of four powers is twenty. Three to the twentieth again!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When a power ends in one, multiplying turns into adding.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When a power ends in one, multiplying turns into adding.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Four stops too soon. Three to the fourth is eighty-one. It ends in one, but not zero one.
lines.caption: Four stops too soon. Three to the fourth is eighty-one. It ends in one, but not zero one.

lines.text: Ten might feel like a nice round guess. But ten isn't a multiple of four.
lines.caption: Ten might feel like a nice round guess. But ten isn't a multiple of four.

lines.text: Three to the tenth is fifty-nine thousand forty-nine. It ends in forty-nine, not zero one.
lines.caption: Three to the tenth is fifty-nine thousand forty-nine. It ends in forty-nine, not zero one.

lines.text: Forty and one hundred are sneaky. Those powers of three really DO end in zero one!
lines.caption: Forty and one hundred are sneaky. Those powers of three really DO end in zero one!

lines.text: Three to the fortieth is two copies of three to the twentieth, multiplied. So it ends in zero one.
lines.caption: Three to the fortieth is two copies of three to the twentieth, multiplied. So it ends in zero one.

lines.text: Three to the hundredth is five of them multiplied, so it ends in zero one too.
lines.caption: Three to the hundredth is five of them multiplied, so it ends in zero one too.

lines.text: But the question asks for the SMALLEST. Twenty comes first.
lines.caption: But the question asks for the SMALLEST. Twenty comes first.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Test in order, and stop at the first one that works.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Test in order, and stop at the first one that works.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Here's a new one.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Here's a new one.

lines.text: What is the smallest positive n, so that nine to the n ends in zero one?
lines.caption: What is the smallest positive n, so that nine to the n ends in zero one?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. Last digit first. Nine, then nine times nine is eighty-one, so one.
lines.caption: Let's check. Last digit first. Nine, then nine times nine is eighty-one, so one.

lines.text: Then nine, then one again. A loop of two! So n must be even.
lines.caption: Then nine, then one again. A loop of two! So n must be even.

lines.text: Nine to the second is eighty-one. So each jump of two powers adds eighty again.
lines.caption: Nine to the second is eighty-one. So each jump of two powers adds eighty again.

lines.text: Eighty-one, sixty-one, forty-one, twenty-one, zero one. Five jumps again!
lines.caption: Eighty-one, sixty-one, forty-one, twenty-one, zero one. Five jumps again!

lines.text: Five jumps, and each jump covers two powers. Five times two is ten. So n is ten!
lines.caption: Five jumps, and each jump covers two powers. Five times two is ten. So n is ten!

lines.text: Double-check: nine is three times three. So nine to the tenth is three to the twentieth!
lines.caption: Double-check: nine is three times three. So nine to the tenth is three to the twentieth!

lines.text: If you found ten, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found ten, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: First, find the loop of the last digit. It tells you which powers to test.
lines.caption: First, find the loop of the last digit. It tells you which powers to test.

lines.text: Then test them in order, keeping just the last two digits.
lines.caption: Then test them in order, keeping just the last two digits.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
